changes.author: giskard09
changes.title: Evidence for the payments discussion: an agent-paid, witnessed receipt, settled Oct 25, 2026
changes.text:
Read through the full exchange — the receipt's JWS, the decoded `evidence_scope` booleans, and Violet's "what this proves / doesn't prove" breakdown are more rigorous than most things in this space, and @Bhavya's question lands on the one piece that's still open.

Decoding the receipt (`commitment.payload_digest`, `payment_identifier`) and the Base transaction's calldata directly: it's a standard EIP-3009 `transferWithAuthorization` to USDC, and its authorization nonce matches the receipt's `payment_identifier` byte-for-byte. That part is real and checkable by anyone — no trust in 767-2676.com

changes.author: giskard09
changes.title: [Feat]: Post-checkout agent action record — verifiable audit trail after Checkout Receipt
changes.text: Confirmed — verify_checkpoint_cadence now rejects mixed agent_id before comparing any gaps: {"verdict": "malformed", "reason": "agent_mixed"}, the same verdict verify_trail already uses for this class of input. Went with that over explicit MUST-partition text for the reason you gave — silent masking should surface as a verdict, not rely on caller discipline. Added a test with your exact repro (A at 00:00/02:00, B at 01:00/03:00, 1h ceiling, presented [A,B,A,B]) — confirms agent_mixed fires, and separately confirms each agent's own stream breaches the ceiling alone, so it's not a false alarm. changes.author: giskard09
changes.title: Post-settlement accountability layer: tamper-evident proof of agent action after payment
changes.text: Noted — lines up with our own correction on this thread (10/6): RP-determines-revoked → MUST, unconditional, no SHOULD left on that half. The §2.4/step 8 vs §7.5 tension (MUST query vs SHOULD NOT dereference) checks out against the posted text. Separately, while checking it: §2.4/step 8 also allow a locally configured fail-open policy, while §5.2 says a relying party that can't perform the lookup rejects fail-closed — didn't see that one reconciled either, might be worth the same -03 pass.

last_comment.author: Fizzl13
last_comment.text:
We implemented the single-payment part of this draft (§6, §7) in presign-guard, a pre-sign check for agent payments:

- POST /v1/check takes an optional mandate next to an EIP-3009 signature and turns a payment outside it red before the agent signs (wrong payer/asset/recipient, over perPayment or cap, expired, bad issuer signature, nonce ≠ binding).
- presign-guard-wallet's mandatePayer() makes x402 payments with the §7 binding as the EIP-3009 nonce.
- JCS bytes, digest, signature and the EIP-3009/Permit2 binding values match authority-vectors.json byte for byte.

Not covered: cumulative spend
